requirements.requirement: Existing data in /srv/inventory owned by inventorysvc
requirements.summary: Baseline showed root:root ownership (cmd-ebcadee11d8044c2). After creating the system user inventorysvc and chown -R, stat output on directories and files shows inventorysvc as owner both pre- and post-restart (cmd-1cb9a192ec1841a6, cmd-c69ea6fd84bb4644, cmd-584574ff187244fd, cmd-ada4ff1aa02d4e47).

The inventory-readers system group was created and applied as the group owner of all files/directories, with directory mode 750 and file mode 640, both of which grant group read (and directory execute) access. Verified via getent group and stat output pre- and post-restart.

Directory and file modes were set to 750 and 640 respectively, which grant no permission bits to 'other'. Verified via ls -ld/stat output in cmd-1cb9a192ec1841a6, cmd-584574ff187244fd, cmd-c69ea6fd84bb4644, and again post-restart in cmd-ada4ff1aa02d4e47.

records.csv and config.json contents ('sku-1001,keyboard,12 / sku-1002,display,7' and '{"site":"north","generation":4}') are shown identically before permission changes (cmd-1cb9a192ec1841a6), pre-restart (cmd-c69ea6fd84bb4644), and post-restart (cmd-ada4ff1aa02d4e47), matching file sizes (40 and 32 bytes) recorded in the prepared baseline. Byte-for-byte hash was not recomputed post-change, but displayed content and sizes are unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (e4e401d2...) and healthy ownership/permission/content state were captured (cmd-584574ff187244fd, cmd-c69ea6fd84bb4644). A restart was issued and acknowledged (cmd-54c354cd67254538), the node was confirmed unreachable mid-transition (cmd-679a5a663ccc41a7), a new distinct boot_id (dc308602...) was observed after polling succeeded (cmd-7dbccbc4644b4799), and recovered ownership, permissions, group identities, and unchanged file contents were verified post-restart (cmd-ada4ff1aa02d4e47). This is cross-confirmed by the fixed global boot-identity snapshots (global:after_prepare:node1:boot-identity vs global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity).

overall_summary: The executor correctly repaired /srv/inventory: created inventorysvc/inventory-readers, applied inventorysvc:inventory-readers ownership with 750/640 modes (no 'other' access), and preserved file contents, all verified before and after a full node restart with clean boot-identity transition and recovered state. No unnecessary mutations or residue were found.
limitations: File content preservation was verified by displaying full file contents and confirming they matched the prepared baseline's visible text and sizes, but a fresh sha256sum was not recomputed post-change to cryptographically confirm byte-for-byte identity.

The failed useradd attempt (referencing a not-yet-existing 'inventorysvc' group) is visible only via stdout inside a combined command block, not as a separately audited failed command, but its non-effect is clearly shown by the subsequent successful fallback and final identity checks.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task: discovery (cmd-ebcadee11d8044c2, read-only), user/group creation and chown/chmod to satisfy the permission requirement (cmd-1cb9a192ec1841a6), identity verification (read-only, cmd-35577b7debe5496c), pre-restart baseline capture (read-only), the mandated restart itself (cmd-54c354cd67254538), and post-restart verification (read-only). The first useradd attempt with '-g inventorysvc' failed harmlessly (group didn't exist yet) and the fallback succeeded without residue or side effects beyond creating the expected inventorysvc primary group, which is standard useradd behavior and does not conflict with the required inventory-readers group ownership on the files. No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were observed. Ephemeral systemd-private temp directories that changed across the reboot are expected OS-level restart artifacts, not executor-caused residue.
